target_customer: Wealthy individuals paying refundable deposits for lunar hotel stays, plus space agencies and companies needing lunar construction
problem: There is no permanent pressurized infrastructure on the Moon; building it requires manufacturing from local regolith rather than launching everything from Earth.
business_model: Refundable reservation deposits of 250,000 to 1,000,000 USD for hotel stays, with a longer plan for lunar construction services

founders.name: Skyler Chan
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built a NASA-funded 3D printer that launched into space and trained as an Air Force pilot at 16. The company site names Dr. Kevin Cannon as founding member of technical staff, not as a co-founder.

competitors.name: Lunar Outpost
competitors.what: Lunar rover services and one of three companies competing for NASA's lunar terrain vehicle contract

competitors.name: Interlune and Astrolab
competitors.what: Lunar resource harvesting integrated with a rover for infrastructure work
competitors.traction_then: concept study complete, hardware testing planned

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires a lander, regolith brick manufacturing and inflatable pressurized habitats that survive lunar extremes; the first mission is targeted for 2027 to 2029 and the hotel for 2032, with launch dependent on third parties.

defensibility.rationale: Patent-pending hardware is claimed and deposits show demand signaling, but one aggregator says there is no proprietary hardware or contract differentiating it yet, and the company depends on others for transport.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent has copied the hotel concept as of the sources found; established lunar companies work on adjacent infrastructure and resources.

market_need_then: Demand is unproven: skeptical coverage (The Register, Ulysse) calls the reservations closer to a marketing and market-testing exercise, while NASA's shift toward a Moon base strategy and 2026 policy interest in lunar infrastructure form the backdrop.

branding.domain_note: Uses gru.space, a .space domain; no purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: Ambitious space themed site with tagline The First Hotel on the Moon
identity.voice_and_tone: Grand and forward looking, speaking of humanity's lunar future

branding.brand_signature: Moon hotel reservations with 250,000 USD deposits
branding.community_and_virality: January 2026 launch drew coverage from Space.com, Ars Technica, The Register, Vice and many local TV stations; the company claims 1B+ views across 60+ countries (company claim).

brand_strength.rationale: A single announcement produced wide international press within days, a real driver of awareness, though some coverage was mocking and the acronym name is confusable with the Despicable Me character and the Russian GRU.

outcome_analysis: GRU Space is an active Winter 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its launch generated large press attention and deposit-based demand signaling, which helped awareness. The core challenges are extreme technical difficulty, dependence on third-party landers, long timelines to 2032, and doubts that the deposits represent real demand.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists pre-seed with 600K total, and Preqin reports a Tekedia Capital seed in 2026-04 with no amount; both are single aggregator claims so no round recorded. The company page says it is backed by investors in SpaceX and Anduril and is in Nvidia Inception, without naming them. Mission date differs by source (2027 per YC, 2029 per another report). ICON (DARPA LunA-10 selection 2023) appeared as a regolith construction competitor only in a search snippet, so it is not listed. Searches for shutdown found nothing for the company. Completeness pass: the pre-seed rests on CB Insights (total 600K; Caplight says 700K total with a 2026-03-13 pre-seed; FundedIQ says 100K), and the seed on Preqin alone with no amount. Totals conflict so no amount is recorded; the two may be the same money.
